land.text: Łęczyca and its castles, set aside by Bolesław III's testament as the dower of his widow Salomea

predecessors.note: The Łęczyca Voivodeship page says the later voivodeship was formed from the territory of the Duchy of Łęczyca, which 'had been established after the 1138 Testament of Bolesław III Wrymouth'; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1138.

land.text: 'her province of Łęczyca reverted to the Senoriate' (Salomea of Berg page)

successors.note: Salomea died on 27 July 1144 and the province went back to the Seniorate Province, whose holder, Władysław II the Exile, is drawn by Cliopatria under its Duchy of Silesia row (514 cells, which leaves these 35 cells out). In 1146 Bolesław IV the Curly became High Duke and Cliopatria's Duchy of Masovia 1147 shape (709 cells) holds 34 of the 35 cells. The Silesia and Masovia dossiers should take the land at those two dates.

capitals.note: 'Salomea died at her mansion in Łęczyca on 27 July 1144'; the page gives Łęczyca as the one town of her dower. The coordinates are the town's, not from the page.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1139 shape applied from the testament in 1138: Salomea's dower around Łęczyca

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the row in 1139 but Bolesław III's testament was enacted 'upon his death in 1138' (28 October 1138, Salomea of Berg page), so the 1139 shape is applied one year earlier. The testament page names the dower only as Salomea's lands ('for life and to revert to the Seniorate Province'); it gives no boundary.

correction.text: The same Cliopatria 1139 shape, valid 1139-1144 only (to Salomea's death on 27 July 1144)

keyframe_review.note: 1139-1146, 8,826 km2 (35 cells: 28 in Łódź, 6 in Masovia, 1 in Świętokrzyskie). The shape is kept but only for 1139-1144: Salomea died on 27 July 1144 and 'her province of Łęczyca reverted to the Senoriate', so the 1145-1146 years Cliopatria draws are the Seniorate's, not a separate duchy (successor handover in identity). Area check: the Łęczyca Voivodeship infobox gives 4,080 km2 for the later voivodeship (established 1339 or 1352), Cliopatria 8,826 km2, a ratio of 2.16; the infobox measures a different, later unit, and the Testament page names no Sieradz or other adjoining land for the dower, so the shape cannot be tested further. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1139..1144 from this entry's own 'valid 1139-1144 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: the town of Łęczyca, several castles and towns: the dower of the widow Salomea of Berg

ledger.note: 1138: Bolesław III's testament sets aside Łęczyca as the dower of his widow Salomea of Berg. 'Bolesław III died on 28 October 1138'; 'In addition Salomea received the town of Łęczyca, several castles and towns throughout Poland'; the Testament page adds that she held the lands 'for life and to revert to the Seniorate Province upon her death'.

region.text: the town of Łęczyca, several castles and towns: the dower of the widow Salomea of Berg

ledger.note: 1144: Salomea dies and her province of Łęczyca returns to the Seniorate. 'Salomea died at her mansion in Łęczyca on 27 July 1144'; 'In accordance with the will of Boleslaw III, her province of Łęczyca reverted to the Senoriate.' The Seniorate was Władysław II's (Testament page); Cliopatria draws it under its Silesia row.

region.text: the town of Łęczyca, several castles and towns: the dower of the widow Salomea of Berg

ledger.note: 1144: the dower ends with Salomea's death and the land passes to the Seniorate Province. Cliopatria's row runs to 1146; the page gives no separate duchy after 1144 and the Łęczyca Voivodeship page dates its own foundation to 1339 or 1352.

notes: eu-15-d, Duchy of Łęczyca. One Cliopatria shape (1139-1146, 35 cells, 8,826 km2). The pages put the end in July 1144 (Salomea's death, the province 'reverted to the Senoriate'), two years before the Cliopatria row ends; the dossier ends in 1144 and hands the 35 cells to duchy-of-silesia, because Cliopatria draws the Seniorate of 1139-1146 (Władysław II) under that row, and the Silesia shape itself leaves the 35 cells out (checked with the gazetteer: zero overlap). Two years of the map therefore depend on the Silesia dossier taking this land in 1144 (it has no matching gain event), and on the Masovia dossier, which holds the cells from 1146/1147 (its ledger carries the 1146 gain of the Seniorate, Silesia and Łęczyca from Silesia). The later Duchy of Łęczyca of 1231-1339 (Casimir of Kuyavia's and Ziemomysł's line, Sieradz and Łęczyca under Leszek of Sieradz) is not in Cliopatria and no page opened covers it (the Łęczyca Voivodeship page is silent 1231-1339); a dossier for it would be a new state for eu-15-x. The Congress of Łęczyca (1180) is in the Casimir II page, not drawn here. No war is listed: the only fighting the Salomea page mentions (the deposition of Władysław II by his half-brothers after 1145, Bolesław IV High Duke in 1146) lies after the dower ended and names no fighting in Łęczyca. Names the gazetteer lacks: Łęczyca, Sieradz (places); the 35-cell shape is used by Cliopatria reference instead.
